Gboard Emoji Kitchen Flags, Browse UI and AI Ranking

Find the flags related to Emoji Kitchen discovery, zero-state suggestions, animation and embedding-based ranking.

What you should know

Emoji Kitchen has separate browsing, suggestion, animation and ranking systems; one toggle rarely controls the entire experience.

Evidence standard: these are real catalog identifiers, but their effects can be inferred, version-specific, or gated. Check the confidence and APK notes before changing settings.

Separate the content from its entry points

Emoji Kitchen can involve suggested emoji combinations, a browsing panel and contextual chips. enable_emoji_kitchen_browse_entry_point_v2 suggests a revised way to enter browsing, whereas enable_emoji_kitchen_for_zero_state_emojis concerns suggestions without a typed query. A visible control does not guarantee the associated sticker assets or ranker are ready.

Why multiple model names appear

The catalog contains references to an embedding index, TensorFlow Lite emoji prediction and a Gemma embedding ranker. They are clues to different techniques used in searching or prioritizing expressive results. They should not be conflated with a full chatbot running inside the keyboard or evidence that every device downloads a large model.

Test discovery and rendering separately

Try opening Emoji Kitchen directly, then compare suggestions after typing the same short phrase. Note whether a combination appears, whether a search result ranks differently and whether an animation plays. These are independent observations; testing them individually produces much more useful bug reports than saying 'Emoji Kitchen works.'

Frequently asked questions

Does a Gemma flag mean the whole keyboard uses Gemma?

No. The identifier concerns a specific embedding/ranking function, not necessarily text generation.

Can I unlock every sticker with one flag?

Not reliably. Asset delivery and feature availability can be independent of browsing controls.
